analysis:
Jalayagnam was described in opposition and media accounts as an election promise by Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy to bring 8.2 million acres under irrigation within five years, launched after the Congress government took office in 2004.

The Hindu reported in April 2009 that about Rs 40,000 crore had been spent, 12 projects had been completed and irrigation had been provided to 18 lakh acres, against a target of adding roughly one crore acres. The programme was also the subject of corruption allegations from opposition parties, which the government rejected.

Against the stated five-year, 8.2 million acre target, the acreage reported by 2009 was a small fraction.
notes: The exact date of the promise is uncertain; day is set to the first of May 2004 (when Reddy took office). The YSR Congress URL was seen in search results and was not fetched directly.
